I will keep my land arranged in the way I can still manage at my age and with some family labor working off-farm. I will put 6 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and keep 3 mu in cotton. I will do that because wheat and maize are my steady grain crops, I have well irrigation, and I know this rotation well after many years. I will keep cotton on a smaller area because it takes more hand work and more spraying, but I still want it for cash income. I will not push for the highest possible input level. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps stand establishment and yield, but I will keep fertilizer and irrigation at a level I believe I can afford and manage. For wheat, I will use moderate fertilizer, irrigate a couple of times, and use rotary tillage because it is easier and saves labor. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 6 mu with hybrid seed, keep fertilizer a little stronger on nitrogen, and irrigate when the crop most needs water. For cotton, I will stay with moderate area, use improved seed, irrigate several times if rainfall is short, and spray more often than grain crops because insects are usually a bigger problem there.
